content.user_title: Explore Local Activity Logging with Nex Life Logger
content.value_statement: Remembering past work and finding visited pages can be difficult without an activity trail. This guide describes local activity indexing and queries; runtime components are not included.
actual_capabilities: Describes indexing browser history, active window titles, and YouTube watch events in local SQLite storage.
Explains activity queries for reconstructing a past time interval.
Outlines daily or weekly summaries by project or application.
Documents search filters for dates, activity types, and browsers.
Explains the stated local-storage policy and optional LLM provider configuration.
limitations: This folder contains only a public guide; scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.
Browser support depends on local history formats.
The described workflow captures metadata, not screen content or typed text.
Runtime privacy claims cannot be verified here; LLM features require separately configured provider access.

use_cases.title: Reconstruct Billable Work
use_cases.description: Freelancers can use the documented workflow to review recorded work intervals before preparing timesheets, once runtime components are separately installed.

use_cases.title: Find Previously Viewed Resources
use_cases.description: Researchers can plan searches across recorded pages and YouTube events when they remember a topic or date but not a title.

use_cases.title: Review Application Time
use_cases.description: Developers can use the described daily and weekly summaries to examine recorded application and project activity.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which activity types Nex Life Logger describes and which runtime components are missing from this folder.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before adopting the workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a History Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the guide, identify filters for finding a YouTube video viewed last week. Do not invent command syntax.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a focused search without assuming undocumented commands.

prompt_templates.title: Reconstruct a Work Interval
prompt_templates.prompt: Using only activity records I authorize and provide, summarize yesterday from 2 PM to 4 PM. Separate observed events from inferred time allocations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review available activity records after separately arranging data access.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Provider Privacy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the guide's local-storage claims and optional LLM provider behavior. List implementation evidence needed before transmitting activity metadata to any provider.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced privacy review before enabling external processing.

output_examples.input: What was I doing between 2 PM and 4 PM yesterday?
output: Illustrative summary from the guide, not retrieved personal activity:
Browsed React and Tailwind CSS documentation in Chrome.
Worked in VS Code on the auth-module project.
Watched a 15-minute YouTube video titled Advanced TypeScript Patterns.

output_examples.input: Where would my activity data be stored?
output_examples.output: The guide describes a local SQLite database and optional LLM provider configuration. No database implementation is included, so actual storage and transmission behavior require verification.

best_practices: Review separately obtained runtime components before granting access to browser history or active window metadata.
Use only records you are authorized to access, and verify inferred durations before preparing invoices.
Review provider data handling before enabling LLM features or sharing sensitive activity metadata.
anti_patterns: Treating this guide as an installed, functioning activity collector.
Assuming activity metadata proves continuous work or exact billable time.
Sending private browsing history to an external provider without informed authorization.

faq.question: Does this folder include a working logger?
faq.answer: No. It contains a public guide, without the original scripts, extension source, or templates.

faq.question: Which activity types does the guide describe?
faq.answer: It describes browser history, active window titles, and YouTube watch events.

faq.question: Does it record keystrokes or screen content?
faq.answer: The guide explicitly says it does not. The missing implementation prevents independent verification of runtime behavior.

faq.question: Does activity data leave my machine?
faq.answer: The guide states that data stays local unless you configure an LLM provider. Review actual implementation and provider settings before relying on that claim.

faq.question: Can searches be filtered?
faq.answer: The guide describes date, activity-type, and browser filters. It does not provide executable search command syntax.

faq.question: Will every browser work?
faq.answer: Browser support depends on the history format available on your machine. The guide does not list supported browsers or versions.
